source.title: Sliding Networks: A Family of Residual Structures Preserving Feature Learning and Feature Diversity

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether architecture shape changes language-model loss at fixed parameter counts and reports substantial shape-dependent differences, qualifying the claim that shape matters little.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling laws and compute-optimal allocation from prior work but does not itself sweep language-model size, tokens, or compute to fit or test those laws. Its language-model results relevant here compare architectures at fixed parameter budgets. HellaSwag is recorded separately because it is a downstream measure, not a test of predictability with scale or pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: The study does not test scaling laws. It does compare language-model loss across depth/width allocations at matched parameter counts: GPT-2 at 124.5M parameters in 1/2/4/12/24 stages, and Tiny Shakespeare Transformers in fixed-capacity depth scans. These results bear directly on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that approximating a continuous-depth (ODE/SDE) limit does not guarantee better finite-model performance, and that the best width–depth allocation is task- and recipe-dependent. In the single-seed Tiny Shakespeare Half Copy scan one wide block gives the lowest training loss, while in GPT-2 twelve or twenty-four stages substantially outperform one at matched parameters and tokens. They say they lack a theory for when depth should beat width.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests residual-architecture regrouping and depth/width allocation, not the original scaling-law fitting procedure or compute-optimal allocation method.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured loss varies with depth and regrouping; Tiny Shakespeare results also vary by recipe, and Half Copy regrouping changes layer-local initialization groups.

fits_no_version.finding: HellaSwag accuracy varies across GPT-2 depth regroupings at the same parameter count: 0.281 for 1 stage vs 0.309 for 12 stages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameter count, depth/width allocation affects zero-shot downstream accuracy. This is not a test of predictability from scale or loss.

record.problems: The GPT-2 shape comparison uses one seed and reports no uncertainty estimates; the authors state that the CE/HellaSwag ordering between 12 and 24 stages does not establish a significant advantage. The Tiny Shakespeare fixed-capacity scan is single-seed and evaluates training windows rather than held-out data. Several other depth comparisons change initialization grouping as well as depth.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant outcomes omitted. The wider CIFAR-10 and Tiny Shakespeare scaling-recipe comparisons were not extracted as separate rows because they change several recipe components and do not isolate architecture-shape effects; see Fig. 6 and Appendices G.2 and H.3-H.4.

Shape effects are measured at a single scale per comparison. Held-out loss is available only for GPT-2 at one size and one seed. There is no systematic aspect-ratio or attention-head sweep.
The CIFAR-10 and Tiny Shakespeare recipe comparisons do not fit loss power laws.
HellaSwag is measured only across shapes at fixed size, not against scale or pretraining loss.
No fitted exponents or comparison of fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. V4 evidence comes from experiments aimed at residual-network scaling limits, not at testing Kaplan's shape claim. Caveats: the GPT-2 results are single-seed; the Tiny Shakespeare results are training-window (not held-out) loss on a small corpus, where memorization may dominate; and Half Copy depth scans change the initialization law along with depth. Moderate shape changes (4–24 GPT-2 stages; depth 20–100 on Tiny) move loss by only about 0.5–4%, consistent with V4. Extreme shallow allocations move it by 5–38%, which qualifies the range over which V4 holds rather than refuting it. The record's state labels used an inconsistent direction convention; they are corrected above. The record's rows_left_out statement that nothing relevant was omitted is inaccurate: see missing.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining-loss power-law sweep over parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or tests of extrapolated losses on larger runs.
No compute-budget sweep estimating optimal parameter and token allocations.
The paper tests selected architecture changes at fixed parameter budgets, not a broad architecture sweep; Tiny Shakespeare results are training loss, and the GPT-2 comparisons are single-seed.
CIFAR-10 and character-level experiments concern residual-network scaling recipes, not tests of the same loss power law across modalities or training regimes.
HellaSwag is measured across shapes, but the study does not test downstream performance predictability with scale or pretraining loss.
The study does not fit or compare scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits under different fitting choices.
